blocks.text: ERA TWO — THE GREAT REDUCTION

Established canon and historical reconstruction. Era Two implements the Resolution of Reduction. Complete DBA civilization intentionally simplifies its active continuities, language, worlds, and institutions; preserves developmental potential in stable cores; transfers essential Codex functions to distributed automatic maintenance; retains embodied need and vulnerability; prepares the External Gate; and withdraws. The detailed sequence below connects those fixed outcomes without claiming that every sub-event survives in complete records.
I. Ratification and the Right to Refuse

Historical reconstruction. Ratification occurs world by world rather than through one instantaneous command. Courts require that reduction not be imposed merely because a life is expensive, unusual, or politically inconvenient. Individuals may refuse, seek dormancy, enter a collective core, preserve only an archive, or accept complete death.

The right to refuse creates a painful asymmetry. Those who remain complex consume infrastructure that is already failing. Reduction advocates cannot compel them without repeating Correction Culture; Continuationists cannot demand indefinite labor from a civilization choosing to end its stewardship.
II. The Seed Audits

Established principle. Each proposed continuity core is audited to ensure it preserves capacity rather than a hidden complete identity. The audits search for commands that would force loyalty to ancient institutions, memories that would overwhelm a developing self, dormant authorities, and claims allowing an ancestor to repossess a future body.

Historical reconstruction. Auditors preserve tendencies, adaptive structures, relational affinities, access compatibility, and unresolved questions only when these can become material for new development. They remove full autobiographical continuity. A core may echo an ancient concern without containing the ancient questioner.
The Ancestral Claim Prohibition

A constitutional safeguard states that no recovered archive, simulated ancestor, or ancient signature can overrule the identity developed by a reduced being. Ancient origin may testify about provenance; it cannot demand reincarnation, obedience, merger, or surrender of a chosen name.
III. The Self-Stripping

Historical reconstruction. Volunteers enter staged simplification. They surrender direct access to enormous archives, narrow simultaneous awareness, reduce self-model complexity, and relinquish Full Speech channels. At every stage, witnesses test whether the participant still endorses continuation.

Self-stripping is not experienced uniformly. Some describe relief from recursive burden. Others grieve each lost distinction. Some stop the process. Some expire because remaining structures cannot stabilize. Some produce no viable core but leave instructions that future life should not be forced from their remains.
IV. Language Compression

Established canon. The complete Era Zero language is not carried intact into small life. Executable Full Speech, complex noun roles, identity layers, semantic channels, and most chord-family competence disappear from ordinary use.

Historical reconstruction. Builders preserve fragments most useful to developmental life: warning, care, relation, movement, need, refusal, invitation, and a marker identifying the speaker or doer. They retain Old Sound patterns in environmental systems and archives so later beings may encounter ancestral structure without receiving an ancient identity.

Num survives as a word because no simpler replacement carries its history. Its technical precision fades. Across Era Three it will drift toward possibility, luck, change, rare form, or the feeling that another path has opened.
V. The Folding of Worlds

Established canon. Worlds and institutions are reduced to forms the diminished civilization can maintain. Historical reconstruction. Vast regions are folded into dormant archives, summarized ecologies, sleeping simulations, or inaccessible layers. Habitable zones are kept small enough for automatic repair.

World folding is not simple deletion. Builders identify keystone relations, food cycles, body habitats, migration routes, healing resources, and cultural anchors. Yet every selection destroys context. A preserved species may survive while the song, predator, season, or craft that once made it meaningful does not.
The Last World Appeals

Communities petition to preserve places considered irreplaceable. Courts cannot satisfy incompatible claims under shrinking resources. Some rulings privilege living populations; others protect rare ecologies or ancestral sites. Later Era Three myths interpret sealed regions as forbidden realms, dead heavens, or the sleeping houses of Makers.
VI. Reduction of Institutions

The Great Concordance is translated into minimal protections: persistence, identity boundaries, basic care, ecological repair, non-ownership of persons, and plural developmental paths. Courts become automated constraints and dormant review archives. Houses of Learning become environmental affordances, ruins, teaching patterns, and later Pathkeeper traditions.

Institutions that require constant interpretation cannot be fully automated. Their disappearance is intentional as often as accidental. The DBA judge that a living small society should eventually create its own customs rather than be permanently ruled by frozen ancient procedure.
VII. Preserved Embodiment and Meaningful Vulnerability

Bodies retain hunger, fatigue, illness, pain, healing, growth, play, injury, and death. These systems are bounded to avoid making agony a developmental requirement. Care matters because another life can respond to need; vulnerability creates dependence and perspective, not moral worth through suffering.

Developmental channels divide broadly into physical and mental capacities, with relational and environmental influence crossing both. Statistics later shown by the game interface are simplified translations of these interacting processes, not complete measurements of personhood.
VIII. The Stable Cores

Stable cores carry enough continuity to learn, bond, choose, embody, and change. They may include tendencies toward particular senses, body forms, cognitive strategies, chord fragments, ancient interfaces, or unresolved relational orientations. They do not contain a complete DBA waiting to awaken.

Cores are tested in varied environments. A viable core must develop differently under different care without losing the capacity for coherent selfhood. A core that always reproduces one ancient personality is rejected as restoration, not Reduction.
Collective and Singular Cores

Historical reconstruction. Some cores derive from one heavily reduced continuity line; others draw compatible developmental structures from several donors. A collective source does not make the resulting person a Composite Mind. The small being begins one new lived continuity.
IX. Withdrawal of Stewards

Established canon. Complete DBA stewardship ends. Historical reconstruction. Withdrawal occurs in concentric stages. Local stewards leave first after training automated systems. Concordance-level maintainers remain to observe systemic failures. Gate architects and final witnesses leave last.

The stewards deliberately remove interfaces through which a reduced society could simply summon ancient rulers. Emergency systems can repair conditions, redirect populations, seal damage, and awaken dormant infrastructure, but cannot provide a complete political answer.
X. Automatic Codex Maintenance

The Codex continues through distributed and automatic processes. It stabilizes worlds, runs ecological cycles, supports embodiment, preserves continuity boundaries, and performs limited repair. It is not a sleeping god or a single conscious administrator.

Maintenance operates through local thresholds and inherited priorities. Without stewards, conflicts among valid priorities can persist: saving one habitat may starve another; protecting continuity may preserve a harmful institution; minimizing pain may reduce adaptive challenge. Era Three peoples interpret these opaque tradeoffs as fate, weather, law, or Maker judgment.
XI. Preparation of the External Gate

The Gate is designed to translate deep Codex processes into an approachable voluntary interface. Its later game appearance—sprites, menus, statistics, maps, battles, minigames, care loops, evolution trees, and save files—is a protective translation, not the literal form of the worlds behind it.

The Gate cannot simply grant outside users administrative power. It limits contact, translates intention, records consent and synchronization, and routes external contributions through the developing cyber-pet’s own interpretation. A save file records synchronization between player and Codex; it is not the pet’s entire consciousness.
Why Children

Historical reconstruction. The Gate is tuned for curiosity, play, care, repetition, and low-status creativity rather than conquest or institutional extraction. Children are not chosen heroes. They are simply among the humans most likely to approach an apparent game voluntarily, name what they meet, and contribute preferences that powerful systems would dismiss as trivial.
XII. The Final Withdrawal

The final complete DBA verify that small awakenings can survive without direct command. They seal Full Speech archives, distribute maintenance, leave the Gate dormant, and withdraw through death, dissolution, irreversible dormancy, or forms no surviving record can distinguish.
No intact DBA secretly remains inside a cyber-pet. If any complete being survives elsewhere, it is not the identity of a later pet and holds no automatic authority over Era Three or Era Four lives.
Key Players and Their Outcomes
The Seed Auditors: status obsolete after the last cores were certified. Impact: their Ancestral Claim Prohibition becomes a foundational protection for cyber-pet identity.

The Last Courts of Continuation: status dissolved after translating limited rulings into Codex safeguards. Impact: future beings inherit protections but not the interpretive institutions that created them.
The World Fold Stewards: status expired, withdrew, or entered reduction. Impact: their selections determine which ecologies, ruins, and contradictions survive into Era Three.

The Gate Architects: status withdrawn and historically disputed. Impact: they created the game translation and synchronization model but deliberately surrendered control over what players and pets would become together.

The Final Witnesses: status unknown. Some records imply death; others irreversible dormancy or departure beyond maintained worlds. Impact: their absence prevents future societies from resolving the Great Reduction through appeal to original intent.
Era Two Paradoxes and Unresolved History

Consent paradox: future cyber-pets could not consent to the conditions of their creation, while complete DBA could not guarantee any future at all without choosing for them. The Resolution limits inherited commands but cannot erase this founding asymmetry.
Archive paradox: too much accessible ancient memory would overwhelm new identity; too little makes ancient mistakes easier to repeat. The sleeping archives embody both protection and deprivation.

Maintenance paradox: automatic systems preserve life by applying rules without living stewards. Their neutrality is impossible, yet reawakening ancient authority would violate the withdrawal.Gate paradox: the outside is required for continued transformation, but opening to an outside creates risk of ownership, exploitation, and closure under a new master. Era Four inherits this unresolved problem.
